utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Pnishi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I remind you that the solemn declaration which you made at the beginning of your evidence will continue to apply to the evidence that you give today. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know I had indicated it was the end of the examination yesterday but there is one question if I may just to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you just clarify for us what were the colour or colours of the uniforms worn by the four persons who brought Dulje Duzhmani to your house on the morning of the 27th of April?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two policemen, they were Serb policemen, they were wearing uniform with stripes, with green stripes. One of them, a star on his arm. The two others were wearing masks and a blue to grey colour uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What is the colour, the basic colour of the uniform of the Serb policemen?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main colour was light green with patches. Probably camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for your permission to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pnishi, good morning. I'm Tomislav Visnjic. I represent General Ojdanic, and together with my colleagues, Norman Sepenuk and Marko Sladojevic, I've prepared some questions for you. You are an experienced policeman and you will understand that will we have to verify your statement. That's why we're going to go into some detail, and we beg your patience while we do that. Mr. Pnishi, you provided a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 4th of April, 2002; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The year is 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you spoke about the events that took place in April, 1999, and while you were talking about that, you provided very precise times of those events. My question is as follows: When you provided your statement, did you use any notes, or did you base your story on your memory, on what you remembered?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything which I have reported so far is based on what I have witnessed with my own eyes. This is the only thing I've said.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: You did not have a sort of a diary or your private notes of these events; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The things which I have recounted and I have informed the Court about are things which will be indelible. Even if a hundred years pass by I will always remember them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pnishi. Mr. Pnishi, you are a farmer and before that you worked in the police force; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: How long did you spend working in the police?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From January, 1969, to the 31st of December, 1983.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pnishi, your village, Meja, how large is it? How many inhabitants does it have? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has about 45 houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Were there any Serbs in your village, Mr. Pnishi?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two Montenegrins in our village, only two. Two households.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show the witness Exhibit D -- 3D26? Could we have that on e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And while this is being done, Mr. Pnishi, I would kindly ask you to look at a new kind of map which provides more detail than the one Mr. Stamp showed you yesterday. I would kindly ask you to help me with understanding some of the things on the map. Mr. Pnishi, this is a map of the general area of your village. How far is your village approximately from the centre of Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our village is some three kilometres away from the centre of Gjakova. Less than three kilometres, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: That's right. Your village is here depicted as Meja Orize village, am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right, because they are kind of adjoining one another. But Orize has only four or five villages. It's more of a -- sorry, houses. It's more of a hamlet. But they kind of overlap, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown the following page of this exhibit. Again this is 3D26, page 2 thereof. Mr. Pnishi, this is the same map, somewhat enlarged. I would like to draw your attention to the two blue, I believe that they are blue, two blue lines that cross the map. Under one of them is says Trava and under the other one it says Erenik. Are these the two rivers that flow through your village or either near it?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My house is between Trava and Ereniki.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can the witness please be shown page 3 of the same exhibit, which is 3D26. Again, this is an enlarged map, the same that we saw before. Are there any technical possibilities for the witness to make some markings on this map or not? I believe there are. Mr. Pnishi, I would kindly ask you, with the assistance of the usher, to put a circle around the area that would approximately depict the place where your house is, the school as well. Can you make a circle around the general area of the area where you lived, where the school was?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The school was approximately at the beginning of Meja, here, and the beginning of Orize. Somewhere here. Can I mark it here on the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Make a circle, if possible, to encompass all those things, the school, your house, the houses of the Serbs who resided in the village, and other villagers as well. Many?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The school may be situated here, the school. My house is 200 metres away from the school in this direction. The direction of Meja and Orize is here. My house is approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, let me makes things easier for you. You don't have to be precise. You don't have to pinpoint your house. Try to encircle the general area of your village, because later on I'm going to show you even a more detailed sketch depicting your house. That's why I'm asking you now to provide us with a general idea of where your village was.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Meja is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this map be admitted as a separate exhibit? I don't know the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Sabbah, would you give it a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That would be IC 00 -- IC3, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think -- perhaps we could just check. I think the exhibit yesterday was IC3 as well. So perhaps we could clarify the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Sabbah. So I'm told it should be IC4.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, you said that in your village there were two Montenegrin families. What were their family names?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their family names are Prentic, the name Dragan. Further away, one kilometre away, was Stajnovic Bozo, Stajnovic. One was dead and he had two sons and his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, what is the distance between your house and the Prentic house?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance between our two houses is 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, in your statement you mention the house of Pask Markaj your best man. What is the distance between that house and your house, the house of Pask Markaj and your house?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same distance like that of Dragan. There is a bridge, Trava bridge, that separates us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Again 50 metres or somewhat more?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not more than 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well then. Let's go back to Exhibit 3D27.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a short explanation. Since we were not able to carry out an investigation on the spot, we tried to sketch the area that the witness is describing, and we believe that with his assistance we will be able to provide the Trial Chamber with the image of the area where certain events took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, I would like to ask you about this sketch looks a bit unclear at the first glance. However, if you look at the drawing you will see that there are two rivers there, the Trava river somewhat in the middle of the drawing, and the Erenik river which is in the lower part of the drawing.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: There is also the Trava bridge. Can you see it? Another thing that is depicted is the house of Pas Markaj. Can you see that? It is in the upper part of the drawing above the Trava bridge.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, below the Trava bridge there is an explanation which says that the road with -- which encompasses the bridge is the old road to Jahoc and Djakovica, a dirt road. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Below that explanation there are three squares which should represent your house and the neighbour's house, but we'll come back to that. Can you see these three small squares?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Across from that is a square which depicts D. Prentic's house. This is the Serb that you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Above that square there is another square marked as the Sokoli house. That is another family from your village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: To the left from the Sokoli house or the square depicting that house there is another square marked as the store, Sokoli store.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And further, more left of that is a somewhat bigger square under which you can read "the school." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: The long line -- actually, the two long lines at the bottom of the drawing mark the new road towards Djakovica or towards Ponosevac. Can you see that as well?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: On that road there is the Erenik bridge. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And next to that bridge there is a point depicting Pask Sokoli's house.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, would you say that this map, despite all the imprecisions with regard to the distances, more or less reflects the situation that actually exists on the ground in your village, the layout of the village, the roads, the bridges?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, would I like to go back to the three squares that represent your house and the neighbouring houses. Could you please mark on this map by putting number 1 next to your house.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is 50 metres away from Dragan Prentic's home.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Which of the three squares would be the closest to the place where you house is?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one here. I put a cross here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you put number 1 next to that square?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, is your house not across the road on the other side of this dirt road leading towards Djakovica? I assume that -- I don't know the situation too well, that's why I'm asking you. Where it says the macadam road towards Jakovci and Djakovica, there are three squares across that road, across the road from the Prentic house.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It is only 50 metres far from Prentic's home.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: But is the road between your house and the Prentic house?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is only the road that divides us, the road that goes to Jahoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And later on that road goes towards the bridge on Trava; is that right? If we go back to the drawing -- please bear with me. I imagine that my drawing is not that good. Just a moment, please. We have a problem with the transcript. I asked you whether later on this road goes towards the bridge on the Trava. Your answer has not been recorded, so could you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's -- that road passes between my house and that of Prentic, and then to the bridge. It's -- the bridge is only 20 metres away from our houses, that is my house and that of Prentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. Pnishi, I'm sorry, perhaps the proportions are not right on this map. However, if you look at this drawing you will see that between the Prentic house and these three squares that are at the very bottom of the sketch there is a road. Now, I'm asking you, out of the three squares that are next to the wording "put prema Jahocu i Djakovici," which of the squares would correspond to the place where your house is? What do you think? So that the road would be between your house and the Prentic house.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know why you have drawn this here. You didn't need to do that. The house of Dragan Prentic, my house, and then comes the road that goes towards Trava. So I don't understand the existence of this here. I don't know why you have drawn it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, would it assist you if you were able to go over to the witness's position and point out to him on the screen what it is you're trying to clarify with him? I mean, this is an unusual course and is not appropriate in many instances with witnesses. But bearing in mind who this witness is and who you are, it seems to me perfectly appropriate for you to do that if it would assist you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think that would be the best thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We've got to make sure --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please speak into the microphone, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for Judge Bonomy, please. Microphone for the Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, if this is the Prentic house and if this is the road that goes towards Jahoc, which of these three squares would be an approximation of the locality of your house? So this is the Prentic house. This is the road.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is -- this is the house of Prentic, and this small one is three small houses they have, and this road here leads to Jahoc. Trava is here. But -- but it's -- it's very far from the Trava bridge that the house of Prentic has been drawn, because the houses of the Prentic should have drawn the houses closer to the bridge and mine right here. And that of Pask Markaj comes here. They hasn't been drawn exactly as they are on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I should go to see transcript, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There is a large map, I think, in Mr. Visnjic's hand which I think can be put on the ELMO so when the witness is pointing and explaining we can see what he's doing. And once he's identified somewhere, you can just ask him to mark it clearly and we can follow it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Except, was the matter clarified in that exchange, Mr. Visnjic? Was the question of whether the house is across the road clarified in that exchange?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: May I take minute, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as I managed to understand what the witness described just now, my problem lies in the following: This map does not reflect actual distances. It does not depict space properly. So it seems that the three houses should be much closer to the Prentic house. That's the problem I've created with this map now. But I would kindly ask that it remain here, because if we proceed as suggested by Mr. Stamp, we will get to a very wide belt and then we will not be able to have a precise drawing of what I want to ask the witness about at a later stage, because after all, except for the place where his house is, it's pretty clear where the bridge is, where the school is, where Pask Markaj's house is. These are the positions that I need for my further questioning. I can accept that this is not -- his house was not marked properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, his -- one of the points made by Mr. Pnishi is that the Prentic house has been drawn too far from the bridge which is causing the difficulty. So it should be nearer the bridge. Now, were you able to establish in relation to that movement whether one of the three squares accurately represents the witness's house?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I approach the witness again just for a moment, please, just to suggest something?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, can you just speak loudly into the microphone as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Forget about the Prentic house now where it was drawn here. If this first square is your house, where would the Prentic house have to be in relation to your house? So this here is your house. In your opinion, where should the Prentic house be marked?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The houses of Prentic should be one here, one here, one here, whereas mine should be right here. The bridge is here, and then the rest is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Now, let us assume that this is your house and we mark it with a number. We mark it number 2. Can you write number 2 there, please.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you now draw some squares or circles here, whatever is better for you, where the Prentic house is?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: These three dots that are drawn here above the road are the Prentic houses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters can no longer hear Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, please. On this exhibit, the square above which the word Kuca D. Prentic is, is not where the house of D Prentic is. As a matter of fact, the houses of the Prentic family are to the right of that and are marked with three red dots. Thank you, Mr. Pnishi, for your patience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I would kindly suggest that you give a figure to this rather than the dots because there's already confusion caused on account of error in the map and this would give -- this would simplify thing. If we have already 1, 2 it can be given number 3 or whatever number you may kindly please. And I would request the usher, if my Lord Bonomy agrees. Dots will always be a trouble.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, can you mark the Prentic houses with numbers 3, 4, and 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that's -- okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: 5 is not legible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pnishi. Mr. Visnjic. Sorry, do you wish this -- do you wish this to be given a number at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but I think that we will go on working on this document that is, so I'm not sure how far we will go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's give it IC5, then. Is that it? Sorry, I've jumped the gun. Apparently we have to wait until you've finished with the map. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, can you please tell me the following: In your yard or next to your house is the house of your brother Djelaj; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djelosh, yes. Yes. Only a wall divides our houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: How far away is his house from your house?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is only a wall dividing our houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I did not hear the interpretation though. Mr. Pnishi, when you were saying that you moved out of your house and when you went to the village of Jahoc, you actually went to the house of Pask Markaj that is on this sketch. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And in actual fact it is your claim that you went about 100 metres away from your own house. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe. Trava is in between. The Trava is in between there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, you have already testified before this Tribunal; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And you testified in the Milosevic trial on the 28th -- or, rather, on the 30th of August, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: During that testimony, Mr. Milosevic cross-examined you about the attack on the Prentic house in May, 1998; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, all of that is on transcript pages 9228 to 9230, Milosevic transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: During that examination, response was that the attack consisted of the following: Twelve bullets were fired from an automatic rifle at the Prentic house. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: During that examination, you asserted that the house was attacked by the Serb police sometime around 10.30 in the evening. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: During that examination, in response to the allegations made by Mr. Milosevic that it was actually the KLA that attacked the house, you said that the Serb house was attacked by two policemen, that they were firing at the roof of the house, not at the windows, and that you saw all of that from the balcony. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: During that examination, you said that that house was attacked only once, on the 6th of May, 1998. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Pnishi, you ruled out the possibility that it was somebody from the KLA that had fired at that house. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It's a thousand per cent correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, it is my understanding of this sketch that Prentic is your next door neighbour, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are the first neighbour. The nearest neighbour in terms of distance away from my place was Prentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated that from your own house you had an overview of what was going on in their houses or, rather, in their yard. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Am I right, Mr. Pnishi, if I say that from the 6th of May, 1998, from that day onwards Dragan Prentic moved his family out to the centre of Djakovica, and apart from the fact that they would come during the day, they never spent the night any more in their house in the village of Meja?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct. Dragan Prentic, up until the last day that he left the house, he lived in his house. He had a house in Gjakova. He went there. He returned to the village and fed the animals daytime, night-time, lunchtime. And nobody else knew better than I did about this. His whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, that's why I'm asking you. My question to you is whether it is correct that he would not spend the night in his house from the 6th of May, 1998, onwards. I'm not denying the fact that he came every day, that he would feed the cattle and so on.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan and his family were there. The police came to the school in a big lorry, and they stayed there for two hours and a half. They came out onto the road. They fired shots from automatic weapons in the corner of the wall. They got in their cars and their vehicles and they left for Korenica. I've seen them with my own eyes. In -- in the morning, I spoke to Dragan, and he said, "People shot at my house last night," and I asked him who did. "I don't know who shot at us. They wanted to kill us." And I told him, "If they wanted to kill you properly they would have killed you, but they shot at that corner of the wall." And as neighbours, we went to the place where the shots were fired, and then there were teams from Gjakova, from the army, from the police. Everybody came. They -- they were checking, examining from where the shots were fired. They went to see where the cartridges were there. We found the cartridges. And they told him -- and they told the villagers, "Who are you suspecting that fired the shots?" And he said, they told Dragan, 'If we wanted to kill you, we could kill you every day. But we don't want to do that.'" And that's what the whole village said. And then they saw the situation, and after that they left for Gjakova.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, I agree with everything that you have said, but you did not answer my question, and what I had asked you was whether on that day Dragutin Prentic slept in his own house in the village of Meja. Only that. Yes or no? From the 6th of May, 1998, onwards, that is.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He has slept there. 90 per cent of the times of the nights he has slept in his house in the village. Otherwise, when he was on duty or his duty required it, he stayed in Gjakova. But he has stayed in his own home.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And his family, is that what you are asserting?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And, actually, you could follow all of that because you had a view from your yard into his yard, and you can see the situation in his house. Is that what you are asserting to me now?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could see into my courtyard, and I could see into his courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pnishi. Mr. Pnishi, let us move on to the next topic. In your testimony or, rather, in your statement on page 2 in Serbian, page 2 in the English, and page 4 in the Albanian, that is -- I'm sorry, I don't know the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before we move on to the statement, for the avoidance of any doubt, none of the event in May, 1998 is referred to in the statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is not mentioned in the statement, but it is mentioned in the Milosevic transcript, 30th of August, 2002. And this is P2238.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand that. So -- yes. Yes. Thank you. The other matter is, are you now finished with the map, and should it now be exhibited, given a number?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. We can give it a number, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit number IC5, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, but may I ask for it to remain on e-court, because probably we will be going back to it later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I'm, I think, not fully informed of the basis of the Prosecution presentation. It's probably my fault rather than anyone else's, but is the Milosevic transcript part of the Prosecution's presentation of material in relation to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, it is not. I think we'd gone over that yesterday and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So how does it -- how does it become P2228?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It was originally in the notification that it would be a 92 bis (D). I think there was some confusion it was supposed to be 92 bis B and then the B became a D so it was included. But it is not and I think I indicated that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you did indicate that, and I hope that you've not been misled by this situation, Mr. Visnjic. And we haven't spent an hour cross-examining on something that is not part of the case. I assumed you had another purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, even if it were not part of the case, I would like to exhibit it because I will be going back to that time and again. Probably we are going to exhibit it ultimately. The only question now is whether it should be assigned a number by the Prosecution or the Defence, but frankly speaking, I don't think the number matters or that that matters in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It has a number which is P2238, but it has -- and it becomes part of the process because you've referred it, and you've made it clear that it is part of the process. It doesn't need any further introduction. All I was trying to do, and you understand -- I hope you'll understand this in a case that is so lengthy, Mr. Visnjic, that it's helpful sometimes for the Bench to be advised of the purpose of examination when it doesn't bear any relationship to the presentation of the Prosecution case, and obviously you never are obliged to tell us the purpose of your particular line of cross-examination, but I was just trying to be clear in my mind that you were cross-examining on something which had not been part of the Prosecution case, and I'm now satisfied that that is the situation and we can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I just make one little comment, with permission. Now, had the witness denied those facts which the learned counsel has put to him, then the necessity of confrontation with that document would have arisen, but here he has not denied he's only brought in those facts as suggested. So I mean, whether it's exhibited or not is inconsequential. That's what I think. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me make things easier for you. My last set of questions will be connected to what the witness has told us, and I am asking you to bear with me. My last set of questions will be about that, and you will be able to tell for yourself what the witness meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, I apologise for this short break. I would kindly ask you now to look at the statement if you have it before you, page 2, paragraph 4 in the Serbian. Page 2, paragraph 4 in the English. And page 4 in the Albanian. The statement will be brought to you shortly. I'm going to ask you in the meantime as follows: In this part of your statement you describe the operation conducted by the Serbian army in July 1998, and in one sentence you say: "One day, I believe that it was on the 31st of July, 1998, I counted 175 VJ tanks heading towards the border with Albania and towards the villages in the area."

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. On the same day that you mentioned, and I saw and I filmed everything I saw from the second floor of my house. I saw and I counted 175 vehicles of the Serbian army, various kinds of cars from small cars to tanks and -- they went from my house in the direction of Ponoshec, Nec, Smolice, and Junik.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So those were not 175 tanks as it says in the statement. It was a column of 175 vehicles of different types. Am I right in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tanks were in large numbers, but there were also smaller vehicles, but always army vehicles, trucks, lorries. All types of vehicles. As I said, 175, but maybe two-thirds were tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have clarified this for me now. I would also like to ask you whether there was any special reasons for which you decided to take the photo of this military column.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I was thinking that if such a large number of military vehicles were to be used in that small area like our village was, something must be wrong, I thought. So I filmed everything, as I said. And when I left the house, I had hidden the film, but the army had searched my house and they found the film and took it with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: When was your house searched?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 27th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: After the 27th of April, you did not go back to your house, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the 27th of April, we left the house and we didn't dare approach our house for 19 days. It was only after 19 days that I went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pnishi. We'll come back to that many later. Mr. Pnishi, are you positive that there were over a hundred tanks in that convoy or is that just your estimate, nothing more?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure that there were over 100 tanks in that convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did that convoy stay for any time in your village or did it just pass through?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It passed through the village, through the asphalt road, and went to Dur [phoen] village and that's where it was stationed, one kilometre away from Korenica. But other crossroads. Police blocks were -- checkpoints were all over.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Entire convoy; is that correct? You took photos of the entire convoy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire convoy, yes. I had it on video cassette.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: How did you know that the convoy was coming your way? I would assume that being a farmer you did not carry a camera with you at all times. You didn't have it handy in your courtyard at any moment. How did you know that the convoy was coming and that you would want to take photos of it?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't take photos of it in the courtyard or the street because I didn't dare do it. I went up to the second or the third floor of my house, and it was from there that I managed to film everything that was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And you filmed the entire convoy?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the entire convoy from the beginning to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: How did you know that a convoy was coming your way?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my house you can have a view 100 kilometre away. I apologise, 1 kilometre away.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Pnishi. You are saying that you saw a convoy coming your way from a distance of 1 kilometre, that you had a video camera handy, that you went up to the first or the second storey of your house and that you filmed the entire thing. Is all that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I filmed all of it from the second floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pnishi, let me now go back to page 2 of your statement, paragraph 5 in the Serbian, page 2, paragraph 5 in the English, and page 3, paragraph 1 in the Albanian version of your statement. You state that on the 23rd of April, your family and yourself abandoned your house and went to the nearby village of Jahoc. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Does it actually mean that you went only a hundred metres away to stay in Pask Markaj's house? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 23rd it was. That day we went further away, but then we came back some 100 metres away from my house and went to Pask Markaj's house, because earlier on everybody left the village, but then afterwards I returned and stayed closer to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And you stayed in that house all that time until the end of the war. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for over two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, your former wife, Lushe, was sick at the time. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she was sick.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And she could not move; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: She couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: She died after the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: She died after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, is it true that because of the restrictions in the movement and other things your neighbours from the Prentic family brought medicines and other necessities for your wife and other members of your family staying in the Markaj house? Am I right in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. They brought us medicine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, let me go back to your statement again, again page 2, paragraph 5, both in English and Serbian, and paragraph 1 on page 3 in the Albanian. You say that on the 27th of April, 1999, at 6.00 in the morning you returned together with your wife to your house to feed the cattle. Am I right when I say that?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how did your wife get to your house? Did somebody transport her or did you do it in some other way? She was seriously ill at the time, if I'm not mistaken. Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taking her by the hand. I was actually carrying her. I didn't want to leave her alone, and very slowly we moved together, and then we went where we went.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And then you arrived at your house to feed the animals. According to the statement, you had cows, pigs, and chickens; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you also speak about the incident that led to the death of Kole Duzhmani, an inhabitant of Korenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And after that, in your statement you say that you were in your house -- just bear with me for a moment, please. Page 3, the last paragraph in the Serbian, the last paragraph in the English version. You say that on that same day from are house around 9.30 you saw people from Guska and Korenica coming along the road and that they made up a long convoy, and you also describe a certain checkpoint. That checkpoint was at the Meja-Orize-Djakovica crossroad and it had been put up by the police. Am I right in saying all this?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Page 4, paragraph 1 in the English, and part of it is on page 3. Mr. Pnishi, let me ask you this: From Pask Markaj's house, could you see from that house the Meja Orize crossroad? Could you see the main road to Djakovica, Junik, from that house?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was staying at my own home until 11.30. And as I told you, my house is closer to the road than that of Pask Markaj. But even after that time when I moved to Pask Markaj's home, I could see the crossroads and the road Gjakova-Meja that goes to Junik. I could see that because I was staying on the third floor of that house, and I said earlier, the distance between our homes is very small, so it doesn't make any difference in viewing the surrounding terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, you are saying that from Pask Markaj's house you could see the exact same things that you could see from your house, the main road, the crossroads, and the rest of the things; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. On page -- on the same page, you say that when you saw around 10.30 that members of all the forces gathered around the school - and I suppose you could see the school from Pask Markaj's house as well - that you decided to go back to Jahoc. In other words, to flee to Jahoc a hundred metres away to your best man's house. That was at 10.30 on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the same day from 7.00 that the offensive started I was at my own home, until 11.30. When the forces gathered, the police and the army gathered in front of school and they started stopping the people, and they shot the people, from the -- at that time then I left and went to Jahoc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a small linguistic thing here. The statement talks about "godfather," and the translation we're getting is "best man," but obviously you're referring to the same person and all that matters is that that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. And I can see another spot of difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In your statement you say that this was at 10.30, and now you're saying in the transcript that it was at 11.30. Can you please clarify this? I assume that there may have been a mistake. So when did you go back to Jahoc, at 10.30 or at 11.30?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At 11.00. Around 11.00 when I crossed the bridge and went to Jahoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, let's go back to the case of Kole Duzhmani. Is it true that Kole Duzhmani was the owner of the petrol station in Korenica?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that he was one of the richest people in the area?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were other people who were richer than him. He wasn't one of the richest.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: But he did have money. He was well off. Can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he was well off I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: What happened to his body once it was discovered 19 days later? Was he buried?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took the corpse and buried in the cemetery of Jahoc. We were six or seven people that went there, because in the household I was staying we were about 40, 50 people. We went, buried him, and went back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And his body is in the cemetery in Jahoc?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They -- after the war, they transferred the body to Korenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, you said that on the 27th you had fled or went abruptly to Jahoc and that after that you did not dare leave the Markaj house for 19 days. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't dare go in the direction of my house for 19 days. On the 19th day, I made up my mind to go and see if there was anything left unburned in my brother's house, and then I found Pal Markaj [as interpreted] dead, as I said. Nothing was left unburned.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, are you saying that you left your cows, pigs, and chickens for 19 days and that did you not go back to feed them? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had left the door open and they could graze in the fields. The pigs were taken -- were killed by the army, and they took them with them and ate them. The chicken were taken by the Gypsies who also ate them. So we were left without anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pnishi, tell me if I'm right or wrong. I'm putting to you that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I just interrupt a moment? There's a reference there to returning to the house and finding Markaj dead; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No, Duzhmani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Markaj is the name recorded. That should be Duzhmani, should it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Kole Duzhmani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Carry on, please, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, tell me if I'm right when I put it to you that you and your family, much before the 27th of April, left your house and went to stay at the Markajs' house. I'm putting to you that much before the 23rd of April you left your house and you -- and went to the Markaj house to stay there. I'm also putting it to you that on the 27th of April you were not in your house in the morning hours. I'm also putting it to you that Kole Duzhmani was killed at least 20 days earlier than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is my submission that perhaps it would be more appropriate for this witness if each suggestion was put singly and separately instead of bundled into one speech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's undoubtedly correct, Mr. Visnjic. You should put these points separately and start with the proposition that they left the house and went to Markaj's house long before the 23rd of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Your Honour, I wanted to be as concise as possible, but key can take it this way as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you and your family left your house much before the 27th of April -- sorry, the 23rd of April, much before the 23rd of April, 1999, and that you went to the Markaj house? Just say yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. How can I say yes when it's not true? That was the day where -- where I describe the death of Prashevic and then when we left, everything that I have said in my statement. No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, I'm putting to you that Duzhmani was killed at least 20 days before the event that you are describing for us, that you found his body before the 27th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi --

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 27th, Kole Duzhmani was intercepted at the bridge and then brought in front of my house. He came inside, and then the -- the police wanted -- started to beat me up, and he told me, "Be brave," and I couldn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Let's make things as short as possible. I'm putting it to you, Mr. Pnishi, that your complete family, together with the animals, moved to Pren Markaj's house -- I apologise, Pask Markaj's house, and that you feared for the safety, and that's why you left the house very rarely during that whole period. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In saying what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, there are two separate issues there. I think the question whether they left before the 23rd has been answered. Your second point is that they left the house rarely because they feared for their safety; is that right? So perhaps you --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Should put that as a separate proposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, is it correct that having left your house, and I put it to you that it was much earlier than you say it was, that you -- that you left Pask Markaj's house only rarely because you feared for your safety.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have left my home on the 23rd. When they fired at the houses, we went out. On the 27th, at 6.00 in the morning, I went back to feed the cattle. That day -- after that day, as I said, for 19 days I never went back to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, who was with you when you discovered the body of Kole Duzhmani?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We're moving on to something that's slightly different, I think, although I can see the link to the questions you've been asking, but we're already beyond the period for a break. So I think unless you have an objection, Mr. Visnjic, this would be an appropriate place to take the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we'll resume at five past eleven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we've noticed that the witness does not have his statement in Albanian in front of him, so we're having one of our own copies handed over to him. Could the usher please help us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There should be the one he had yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: He has a copy in front of him. That, I think, is his statement in Albanian. I can see from here the stamp of the certifying officer when the declaration was made.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Okay, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The witness says he already has the Albanian version, so return that, please, to Mr. Visnjic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, our questions are going to be very brief now, and I'm going to ask you to give brief answers as well. I put it to you that considerably before the 23rd of April, 1999, you even transferred your livestock to Pask Markaj's house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I'm also putting it to you, Mr. Pnishi, that Kole Duzhmani was killed by the KLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I also put it to you, Mr. Pnishi, that Kole Duzhmani was killed because he did not meet his financial obligations vis-a-vis the KLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true, not at all true.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, who was with you when you found Kole Duzhmani's body?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there with my godfather Fran Markaj and my daughter Valbona Pnishi.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Nobody else as there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Pnishi, now I'm going to move on to page 4 of your statement in which you describe the killing of seven persons on the bridge, on Trava. Mr. Pnishi, on this map that is right in front of you -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, first and foremost, I would like to ask that the witness be shown a new, unmarked exhibit, 3D27.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we also have this enlarged. A bit more, please. A bit more, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, can you mark the place where the bodies were, the bodies of the killed persons?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who stopped them on the road to school, they took them and -- and they killed them right here. They took seven persons from here, and they took them right to the bridge, to the corner of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Could you please mark on this map the place with some number or a mark. Say, put the letter X, or a cross, yes.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the seven people were killed, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: The place where the bodies were when you checked them?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five bodies were right here. So five bodies were on the bridge and two had fallen off the bridge, but five were right here at the corner. Two of the bodies had fallen down. I was on the third floor of Pask Markaj's house, and in aerial distance it's just 15 metres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That answered the question. That's answered the question, and it's marked on the map with a red dot. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And then you say that at 12.00 you went to this place where they had been killed. By the way, were there five or four bodies there?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In all there were seven bodies, and the oldest was no more than 25, 25 and under. I just wanted to ascertain whether any of my sons was among them. I checked them, and I left them there, and then I went back to Pask Markaj's house. So five were on the bridge and two had fallen down from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Two. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, who was with you? Mr. Pnishi, who was with you when you got out of the house and went to the bridge to check this? I mean these bodies.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not allow anyone to follow me, to come with me, because soon after that the police were surrounding the area and I didn't want anybody to come with me. So I went there. I went to the bridge, and I turned the bodies over to check, and all of them were young men, and I saw that no one was any of my sons. Then I went back to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, I put it to you that on the 27th of April, around 2.00, Dragutin Prentic with his wife Jovanka came to Pask Markaj's house. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at 2.00, but it was about 5.00 in the afternoon. It was not in the courtyard of Pask Markaj, but he called, "Pask, Pask," from his own house, and he asked just, "Are you alive?" That's all he asked from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I put it to you, Mr. Pnishi, that with Dragutin Prentic you left the courtyard of Pask Markaj's house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: The same day after 2.00 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. It's true that he called from his own courtyard, "Pask, Pask, are you alive?" That's what he said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I put it to you, Mr. Pnishi, that together with Dragutin Prentic you came to the bodies, that you did exactly what you described. You turned a body to check to see whether it was anyone of your own that had been killed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. That's not correct. When I went to the bodies, I also called for Dragan to come along with me so nobody could kill me, but Dragan could not come. Jovanka, his wife, said, "Wait. I can come with you to there." And I wait until I turned them over, and she had -- she was nearly there, but then when she saw what had happened, then she put her hands on her head very worried and she turned back. She started crying, and she turned back to her house. She couldn't cope seeing such a state of -- such a situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I further put it to you, Mr. Pnishi, that together with Dragan Prentic or Dragutin Prentic, it's the same person regardless of what the transcript says, you left the bridge to see your own house, and after that you returned together with him to the Markaj house. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that day. No, it's not correct. That day the things stand as I described them. He did not come with me. His wife said she was joining, but when she came halfway and saw what had happened, then she put her hands on her head and started crying. She broke in tears.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I put it to you -- actually, Mr. Pnishi, on what day did you go from Markaj's house to your house together with Dragan Prentic if it was not that day?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that day. It was five, six days after that day. Dragan came back from Gjakova together with his wife. They came to the house where I was staying and brought some medicine for me. And the army went into my courtyard. They killed some pigs. They took them away. And from there with Dragan, Dragan said, "Let's go there to tell them not to take stuff." And I said, "Let them do it. It won't help." When we went there, "Why are you taking them?" The army people said, "The army will need them," so they took them away, and we went back with Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Are you telling me now before that -- those 19 days expired you went to your house actually? Before that 19-day period when you said to me that you found the body of Kole Duzhmani in your house, are you telling me now that actually five or six days after the 27th you went to your house?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are confusing me with putting all these dates and times and all that. You're confusing the picture, because before the 27th, we left the house on the 23rd, and up until the 27th I had never been to the house. I was never there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And then five or six days after the 27th, as you said just now, you went to your house with Dragan Prentic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not enter the courtyard or the house which was just on the road outside the gate, because we feared that the army and the police would come. So he went into his house and then we went.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Pnishi, today, at the beginning of your testimony, you said to me - I think that's on page 22 - that after the 27th of April, you did not go back and did not even approach your house for 19 days. That's page 22, line 8 through 14. Now you're telling me that, nevertheless, you did that after five or six days. So am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're not right, because it's not the same as going into the house, entering the house, or just walking past the house and staying on the road near the house. We never entered the house for 19 days. So we didn't do that for 19 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, I see page 22, lines 29 and 30 [as interpreted], and you said that you did not dare approach the house. Have you got anything to say to that?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth is that we didn't dare. But Dragan said that, as he was there, "Let's go together to tell them not to touch stuff from your house," but they'd taken them so we came back. We didn't dare to get even into the courtyard. For 19 days. For 19 days we couldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the transcript, what I said was page 22, lines 12 and 13. So it should not say page 22, lines 29 and 30, as it does say in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you for correcting that, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, as for the bridge where the bodies were, on the left-hand side of the bridge, actually, are there bushes there that are over 3 metres high? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I know the witness is already answering but I rise. I suspect there -- I suspect what my friend wants to ask if, on the 27th, on the day in question, 27th of April, there were bushes here at that time. The question reads there are, as if they were talking about the present. Now, I don't want the witness to be answering one thing when the question means another. I suspect the question relates to the date we're concerned about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you to Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: At the time when the bodies were there, that's the 27th of April, springtime, well into spring, on that side of the bridge, on the left-hand side of the bridge, are there any bushes there and trees that are up to 3 metres high or perhaps a bit above 3 metres? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was something like that near the bridge, and above the bridge, yes, there are trees and bushes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Am I right, Mr. Pnishi, when I put it to you that from Pask Markaj's house you could not see the actual place where the bodies were and that that's why you went out, to have a look?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: How couldn't I not see the bodies when in aerial distance from the third floor of the house it's no more than 50 metres away? How can you say that you cannot see the bridge? You could -- you could -- you could see the bridge even from a kilometre away, because the trees had not vegetated. They had not bloomed. You could not see -- it wasn't -- it was a clear view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, the question wasn't whether you could see the bridge, it's whether you could see the bodies. And it's being suggested that the bodies which would be on the ground could not be seen because of the foliage. What's your answer to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the window from which I was looking from, there is no tree in the way to where the bodies were, to the bridge. I saw them when they fired their automatic weapons. It's only 50 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, what I assert is that it is correct that the bodies were there and that it is correct that there was a total of six bodies there, not seven, but that it is not correct that you saw the killing itself. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that's not correct. There were five bodies on the bridge and two bodies had fallen off the bridge. There were seven all together. I saw them when they lined the people up, when they shot them, and where they fell on the ground. I saw who carried those bodies away from the scene of the killing. I've seen them myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, you stayed in Pask Markaj's house until the end of the war; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. Yes. Sometimes there, sometimes even deeper into the village, but that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, can you explain the distinction to me? Why did you feel safer in a house that was about 50 metres away from your own house?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just a minor thing. Perhaps Mr. Visnjic could indicate where it is that he said that it was 50, because I thought he said it was a hundred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The answer -- he said it was 50 metres but no more than a hundred. So we're talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A hundred metres. I accept. Let me rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, can you explain to us why was it that you felt safer in a house that is not more than 100 metres away from your own house? What's the difference?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever you get an opportunity to get further away from where the bullets are falling you feel a bit safer, because the -- the people were trying to get further away from the concentrated forces, Serb forces, and whoever came on the asphalted road was shot at, and my house is closer to there. And if you manage to get further away from that shooting area it was a bit safer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So there is no special reason why it was precisely Pask Markaj's house except for the fact that it's about a hundred metres away from the road?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where else could I go? Because if I crossed the asphalt road, I might have got killed. So my intention was to go away from the fire, or from the shots as much as I could, even if it was one metre away.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, therefore, you are telling me that it is only natural for people to get away from a place where there is a conflict. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Nobody likes to get killed. They were all innocent people, those who were killed in Cabrat. All of them were all innocent.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, since you mentioned Cabrat, is that the hill that was bombed during the NATO strikes? It was often bombed. It was targeted the most perhaps in all of the Djakovica municipality. Did you have that Cabrat hill in mind?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I meant, the Cabrat hill where every 50 metres you could find a tank stationed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, could you tell me this: As we mentioned already, you testified in the Milosevic case, and at page 9293, during a cross-examination -- excuse me. It was in response to Judge Kwon's question concerning your previous assertion that you understand Russian. You said that the person whom you identified was Russian said something in Russian, something along the lines of "Destroy it." What did that person say in Russian?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I opened the door to them and I told them in Serbian --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pnishi. This is all in your statement. I'm interested in this particular phrase. What did you hear him say in Russian, something that would mean "Destroy it," in English?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Russian didn't understand the name, because they were looking for my brother. But the last name is the same, Kole Djelosh, and Kole Duzhmani. It's similar. So they took him and shot him in the kitchen of my brother's home. They were talking among themselves. They were not talking Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please listen to the question that you're being asked. It's a very -- it's a very specific question. Mr. Visnjic will put it again, but concentrate on that question and please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, what did you hear them say in Russian that would mean "Destroy it"?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't speak Serbian among themselves because I know Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, it's a clear, specific question. Please answer the question you've been asked, which is what did they say in Russian? Never mind the fact that they didn't speak Serbian. Just tell us what they said in Russian.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pnishi, just to remind you. You mentioned that yesterday in your testimony, but it wasn't answered in -- entered into the transcript, although I heard you say that. Could you please repeat what is it that you said they said in Russian? "Destroy it"?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said "unisti." Him. He was outside the yard and he addressed this soldier who was inside my yard, and told him "unisti ga," which means destroy him, liquidate him --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S. And based on your knowledge of Russian, you claim that this was Russian, that this was a Russian phrase.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he said "zdravstvujte," I understood that he was not a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Pnishi?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's certainly not all right with me. Is Unisti Ga Serbian or is it Russian?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe Honourable Judge Kamen could assist you with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think the witness ought to assist us. What is it that you actually heard being said? Was it words which were Serbian or words which were Russian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The word that he said from outside the yard to the other soldier he said in Serbian, "Is Durosh [as interpreted] Kole here?" He said "Tuka je, tuka je." "Unisti ga," said to him, this other guy from outside the yard, and they took Kole Markaj [as interpreted] to my brother's home and shot him. Duzhmani.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And those people were Russian; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN PNISHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am 100 per cent sure that they were Russians because if they had spoken Serbian I would have understood them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Visnjic. And before you carry on, are you finished now with the map which is on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So that gets a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That will be Exhibit number IC6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before it's removed, if it's going to be removed, Jahoc, which is referred to on this map, is in which direction?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the way I understood it, Jahovci is on the other side of the bridge. Perhaps the witness could clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... As we look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As you say, Your Honour, on the other side of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is it immediately over the bridge that you regard yourself in Jahoc or is it further away than that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once you cross the bridge you are in Jahoc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have just a small comment concerning the layout of the terrain.
